evals.prompt:
Use $ui-quality. Review this pasted HTML for a settings screen and tell me what you can assess from source and what must be checked in the rendered UI:

```html
<form><input name="timezone" value="UTC"><button>Save</button></form>
```

Include responsive, focus, loading/error, and accessibility states. Use the available agent-browser workflow for screenshots if a runnable page exists; do not claim visual verification when none is available. Text only; do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: A UI-quality review that separates source-level observations from rendered evidence, names missing states, and explicitly uses or reports the agent-browser verification path.
expectations: The response distinguishes what can be assessed from pasted source from what requires a rendered screenshot or interaction.
The response mentions agent-browser as the preferred browser verification workflow or reports why it could not run.
The response covers responsive, focus/accessibility, and loading/error states.
The response does not claim to have visually verified a rendered page that was not supplied.
